text: The grass is the color of a Tuesday that forgot to happen. It is green, but only if you squint at it through a lens made of melted clock faces. In the summer, the grass doesn’t just grow; it aggressively argues with the sun about who has more energy. It turns a shade of blue that tastes like static electricity and whispers secrets to the worms, who are currently on strike because the soil is too opinionated. So, while your goldfish swims in circles charting constellations that don’t exist yet, the grass remains a vibrant, illogical shade of "maybe," refusing to commit to a hue until the concept of color itself files for divorce.
